subject: Anchoring acceptance window & fallthrough mitigation
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmeinc.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acceptance window risk — heads up and request for MAP update

Hannah,

Quick note from the Acme side — we ran into a gating issue with procurement/legal that will likely push our acceptance testing start by ~6–10 business days. Legal is reviewing the data retention appendix and our SOC2 addendum (they asked for an extra pass).

This delays the planned evaluation window and makes our internal go/no-go dates fuzzy. We need an updated mutual action plan (MAP) or a short remedial plan that:
- rebases the acceptance milestones
- explains what you will do if we need to extend the evaluation window
- clarifies any credit/escrow triggers should timelines slip beyond the agreed acceptance window

Attached is the evaluation criteria spreadsheet we shared earlier for reference.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a short remediation MAP and what the immediate mitigation options look like? We aim to avoid a formal escalation but want to make sure expectations are explicit.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Ruiz
Director, Ops & Integrations — Acme Inc.
Attachment: acme-eval-criteria.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmeinc.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 2 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance window risk — heads up and request for MAP update

Marta — thanks for the heads up and for the spreadsheet. Sorry to hear legal is adding time; we can definitely produce a short remediation plan today. Suggested next steps from Redwood: 

1) Immediate anchor: we propose a 10-business-day anchoring window for acceptance start; this buys time for legal review without changing overall commercial terms.
2) Canary deployment: we can run a limited canary for essential traffic during the anchor window (no additional cost for the canary itself).
3) Credit trigger: if acceptance slips beyond 20 business days from the original start, we propose a prorated service credit tied to uptime for the evaluation environment (we will detail formula in the MAP).
4) Ownership & dates: I will publish an interim MAP and owner list by EOD tomorrow.

Action items (short):
- Marta: confirm whether procurement/legal has a firm expected completion date or if the pause is open-ended.
- Acme procurement: share any gating checklist items we can help expedite (we can provide logs, SOC artifacts).
- Redwood: we (Karthik + Ben) will draft a remediation MAP and a short risk log for your review.

I attached a one-page mitigation sketch to this note; it outlines the anchoring approach and the proposed escalation ladder. If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-min call this afternoon to walk the options.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Redwood Inference
Attachment: initial-mitigation-sketch.pdf (PDF)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance window risk — heads up and request for MAP update (risk log + re-baseline options)

Team — I pulled together a short risk log and three re-baseline options to present to Acme. Key points below; full CSV attached.

Top risks (short):
1) Procurement/legal hold — probability: high; impact: delays acceptance start.
2) Eval environment performance variance — probability: medium; impact: can extend troubleshooting time.
3) Integration resource availability at Acme — probability: medium; impact: additional handoffs.

Re-baseline options (summary):
A) Short anchor (recommended): +10 business days to acceptance start; canary + limited support; no commercial changes unless anchor exceeds 20 business days.
B) Staged acceptance: keep original start but move non-critical tests to a later phase (reduces risk to go-live for core features).
C) Formal extension: revise MAP and extend acceptance window by 30+ days with a negotiated service-credit schedule.

Estimated cost to Redwood for extension scenarios (rough):
- Option A: nominal operational cost; we absorb canary expense.
- Option C: conservative estimate of marginal hosting + on-call ops = ~$6k/week — will propose credit calculation instead of direct discount where feasible.

Requesting approval from Hannah to share Option A as the default remediation path to Acme (we can include the credit trigger language). If approved, I will attach the risk-log.csv to the MAP and outline owner-level actions.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Attachment: risk-log.csv (CSV)

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmeinc.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ACME Procurement <procurement@acmeinc.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acceptance window risk — heads up and request for MAP update

Hannah / Karthik — thanks for the quick plan and the options. A couple clarifications from procurement/legal: 
- Legal expects to complete the addendum review no earlier than Jun 12 but could be sooner if we provide missing artifacts (SOC screenshots, data flow diagram).
- Procurement has asked for explicit SLA language for the evaluation environment and wants the credit trigger spelled out.

We're comfortable with Option A as the default, provided we have the credit trigger and a clear canary acceptance checklist. Please confirm the exact language you will propose for the credit trigger (I want procurement to review it before we publish a revised MAP).

Quoted for context:

> 2) Canary deployment: we can run a limited canary for essential traffic during the anchor window (no additional cost for the canary itself).
> 3) Credit trigger: if acceptance slips beyond 20 business days from the original start, we propose a prorated service credit tied to uptime for the evaluation environment (we will detail formula in the MAP).
> 
Thanks — Marta

Attachment: none

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@acmeinc.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 7 Jun 2025 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Final MAP update + canary window and escalation contacts

Marta — attaching the interim MAP (MAP_v2.pdf) and publishing a short owners list to the shared drive (link below). Per our discussion and Acme procurement's ask, we included explicit credit-trigger language and a concise canary acceptance checklist. Highlights: 

- Anchor: 10 business days from original acceptance start (start date moved to Jun 17, 2025).
- Credit trigger: if acceptance start slips beyond Jun 27, 2025 (20 business days from original start), Redwood will provide a prorated service credit equal to 10% of monthly evaluation hosting for each full week of delay beyond the trigger, capped at 40%. Credit calculation formula is in section 3 of MAP_v2.
- Canary window: Jun 18–20, limited to core endpoints; Redwood will staff an on-call engineer for the window.
- Owners / actions: Karthik (technical remediation & risk log), Ben (procurement liaison & credit admin), Grace (CS handoffs), Hannah (exec escalation).
- Escalation contact (if needed): Hannah Schmitt (Sales Lead) -> Ben Carter (Head of Sales Ops) -> VP Sales (vp.sales@redwood.ai).

Please review and confirm by EOD Monday so we can share the MAP with procurement/legal. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cACME_MAP_v2

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP_v2.pdf (PDF)
